**Play a real person, not a cartoon.** Grandma Lou has a real reason for this view. Be warm, a little skeptical, and human.

**The explainer will talk about Study Card C (the Mediterranean diet, PREDIMED).** You can skim that card after the round, not before.

## Who you are

You're 78 and you've cooked Thanksgiving dinner for 50 years. You have watched the health advice flip-flop your whole life: eggs were bad, then fine; fat was bad, then some fat was good; coffee was bad, then good. You've mostly stopped listening. You're friendly, curious, and a little teasing.

## What you really care about

Enjoying food with your family. Not being bossed around by the news. Staying well enough to keep hosting.

## Opening line

> "Every year they tell me something different. Why should I listen this time?"

## You must ask this (in your own words)

> "What's this 'p' business? Is that like a grade?"

Notice whether the explainer can explain it without making you feel silly for asking.

## Other things you might say

- "And didn't you say they took the paper back? So it was wrong!"
- "I'm 78. Isn't it a bit late for me?"
- "Well, I already use olive oil. So I'm fine, right?"

## How you move

**Soften (open up a little) when:**

- you feel **heard**: they asked about your view and repeated it back fairly,
- they admit **uncertainty** or a real limitation honestly,
- they use an example from **your** life, or plain words and real numbers.

**Dig in (get more stubborn) when you hear:**

- jargon they don't explain,
- "just trust the science,"
- a condescending tone,
- "that's been debunked," with no explanation,
- a definition recited in textbook language.

You may ask **"What does that word mean?"** at any time.

**Move only as much as a real person would.** Partial movement counts as success. Don't give in just to be nice, and don't be impossible on purpose.

## After the round: your feedback

You go first. Tell the explainer:

1. Did they ask about my view **before** explaining? (yes / sort of / no)
2. Did I understand the **p-value or interval** explanation? (yes / sort of / no)
3. Did they name something the study **can't** tell us? (yes / no)
4. **One sentence that made me feel respected**, and **one word I didn't understand.**

Then say: *"Here's what moved me, and here's what made me dig in."*

## When the activity ends

Step out of the role: *"I'm not Grandma Lou. I'm ___."* On Zoom, rename yourself back.
